text:
alex: Quick sync — we need to land per-model/route SLO dashboards that show P50/P95/P99 latency, TTFT, and tokens/sec. Need input from runtime + infra on what fields/tags we can rely on from telemetry.

sam: +1. Can runtime emit route_id/model_id and a routing_policy label? TTFT is calculated at edge, right? or runtime?

priya: Runtime can emit model_id and route_id. TTFT (time to first token) we currently measure in the edge proxy but we can bubble an event to the trace with a tag `ttft_ms`. We should pick one canonical metric name.

maria: Agree we need canonical names. Proposal: `llm_request_duration_ms{quantile="pXX",model,route}` for histograms + `llm_ttft_ms_sum` and `_count` for TTFT summary, and tokens/sec from `tokens_generated_total` (counter) with rate().

kyle: SRE note: high-cardinality labels (route + model + tenant) will explode metrics cost. Can we limit to route + model and optionally a low-cardinality tenant bucket (prod/stage)? :warning:

jen: For dashboard UX, console wants pre-baked panels per-model with a route selector and a global rollup. Also need an annotation when rollouts happen (canary -> prod) so we can correlate regressions.

priya: We can add rollout_id as an annotation event pushed to telemetry; not as a label on every point. That keeps cardinality down.

sam: Good call. For tokens/sec panel query example: `rate(tokens_generated_total{model="gpt-redwood-8k",route="chat"}[1m])` and TTFT p95 via `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(llm_ttft_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, route))`.

alex: That histogram_quantile expression looks right. Can infra confirm ingestion window / scrape intervals so these queries are stable?

ops-bot: Deploy notice — telemetry-ingest v2 rolled to canary at 2026-02-02T09:12:30Z (commit 7f9d). Traces and metrics may be delayed up to 30s.

maria: Ingestion is 15s scrape right now, but Prometheus remote write batching introduces ~20s. We'll standardize dashboards on 1m and 5m rollups to avoid noise.

kyle: Also add a throttling metric: `inflight_requests` and `queue_wait_ms` so dashboards show when routing/batching is adding latency.

jen: UX asks for these panels: latency heatmap, TTFT timeseries (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, throughput (reqs/sec), and a small events lane for rollouts and infra incidents. Can we get sample panel JSON so Console can import?

priya: I'll drop a skeleton Grafana JSON here in a minute. For now here's a minimal set of metric names we'll commit to: `llm_request_duration_ms_bucket`, `llm_request_duration_ms_count`, `llm_request_duration_ms_sum`, `llm_ttft_ms_bucket`, `tokens_generated_total`, `llm_inflight_requests`.

alex: Ownership: runtime owns emitting model/route labels and TTFT events. infra owns ingestion, scrape cadence, and the rollout annotation pipeline. Platform/console owns dashboard layout and UX. Sound fair?

sam: Sounds good. Action items: priya -> produce Grafana panel JSON + canonical metric name doc; maria -> confirm scrape/aggregation windows and cost estimate for route+model dims; kyle -> propose tenant bucketing scheme; jen -> sketch Console import UX and annotation slot.

priya: I'll post the Grafana stub by EOD.

maria: I'll run a cardinality sim and post numbers tomorrow. Initial guess: 200 routes * 30 models -> 6k series per metric, times 10 metrics = 60k series. Could be higher with tenants.

kyle: For tenant bucketing: use `env=prod/stage/dev` + `customer_tier=free/paid/enterprise` as optional. That should keep it sane.

alex: Great — thanks all. tagging owners here @priya @maria @kyle @jen :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Reminder — please file an RFC in /docs for metric naming and retention if this changes billing impact.

jen: I'll create a Console ticket and link the grafana import once priya posts it.

alex: Okay we'll reconvene after the artifacts. TTFT: sync next Wed 16:00 PT. :calendar:
